identity.title: OpenApps: Simulating Environment Variations to Measure UI Agent Reliability

problem.claim: Measure UI-agent reliability across variations in app design and content, not only within one fixed environment.

gap.claim: Fixed-environment evaluations reveal task completion only for specific app environments and can miss deployment-relevant variation effects.

contributions.claim: OpenApps is a lightweight open-source ecosystem of six configurable apps whose appearance and content can vary.
The ecosystem runs on a single CPU and supports generating and deploying thousands of app versions.
Across more than 10,000 evaluations of seven leading multimodal agents, reliability varied substantially across app variations despite relative stability within fixed apps.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors introduce app-variation evaluation as a new dimension for measuring UI-agent reliability, implemented through OpenApps.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that many agents’ task success rates fluctuate by more than 50% across app variations.
The authors report Kimi-VL-3B’s average success across tasks ranging from 63% to 4% across app versions.
The authors report that looping and hallucinated-action behaviors differ drastically with environment configuration.

narrative_sequence.summary: Reliable task completion is necessary for users to trust autonomous UI agents.
Fixed app environments cannot characterize reliability under changing app design and content.
OpenApps provides six configurable apps and low-cost generation of thousands of versions.
The authors evaluate seven multimodal agents in more than 10,000 independent evaluations.
Reliability and failure behaviors can change sharply across app variations, motivating this evaluation dimension.

source_observation.claim: The paper contrasts stable fixed-environment reliability with large variation across configurable app versions, including a 63%–4% example.

lessons.interpretation: A single-environment score may conceal sensitivity to interface and content changes.
lessons.application: Report performance distributions across systematically varied environments alongside fixed-environment averages.
lessons.exception: This may be unsuitable when deployment guarantees a genuinely immutable interface and content.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the variation dimensions, task set, agent identities beyond Kimi-VL-3B, or evaluation metric details.
The abstract does not provide per-agent results or conditions explaining the observed fluctuations.
